prompt_text: I need a personal injury attorney in Chicago after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
Here are five Chicago personal-injury firms you should call after a car accident — and why each is worth speaking to. Call at least three for a free consultation so you can compare answers and feel comfortable with the attorney you pick.

1) Clifford Law Offices
- Why call: One of Chicago’s best-known plaintiff personal-injury firms with extensive experience in motor-vehicle collisions, catastrophic-injury and wrongful-death cases. They have the staff and trial experience to take cases to jury when insurers won’t offer fair compensation.

2) Corboy & Demetrio
- Why call: Longstanding Chicago trial firm that focuses on high-value personal-injury claims, including auto collisions and catastrophic injuries. Known for aggressive trial advocacy and securing substantial settlements/verdicts for clients.

3) Levin & Perconti
- Why call: Chicago-based firm with a strong track record handling serious injury and wrongful-death cases from car crashes. They emphasize client communication and have experience dealing with complicated medical and insurance issues.

4) Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard
- Why call: Trial-focused plaintiff firm that handles auto accidents and catastrophic injury litigation. Good reputation for personal attention and trial readiness; strong in Cook County practice.

5) Simmons Hanly Conroy
- Why call: National firm with a major Chicago presence that handles serious personal-injury matters, including motor vehicle collisions. They have large resources for complex cases and experience litigating against big insurers.

What to look for when you call
- Ask if they handle automobile crash cases in Cook County and nearby counties.
- Ask about experience with cases like yours (severity of injury, liability issues such as rear-end or multi-car, hit-and-run).
- Ask whether they take the case on contingency (no upfront fee; they get paid only if you recover) and what fees/expenses look like.
- Ask who will handle the case day-to-day (partner vs. associate/paralegal).
- Ask their approach: do they settle quickly or prepare for trial?
- Ask for recent sample results for similar cases (they can usually share ranges).

What to have ready for the consultation
- Date/time/location of crash, police report number if available.
- Photos of the damage/injuries, medical records/treatment summary, and insurance information.
- Names/contact info of witnesses, if any.
- A short timeline of what happened and current medical status.

Quick next steps after the call
- Get medical treatment and follow doctors’ instructions.
- Preserve evidence (photos, vehicle, phone video) and get a copy of the police report.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without your attorney.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code, a short description of your injuries, or whether there were serious injuries/death — I can narrow these options to firms very close to you, check practice focus, or prepare a short script of questions to use on your calls.
